questions.prompt: The Nazis once exhibited art they deemed not 'purely German' enough so citizens could view and despise it in person, and the show ended up drawing crowds that outpaced typical art galleries. How many works of art were displayed in this 1937 Degenerate Art exhibition in Munich?
questions.hint: Somewhere between 550 and 900 pieces of art were shown.
questions.explanation: The exhibition featured 650 works of art confiscated from German museums, meant to showcase 'degenerate' modern art that the Nazi regime condemned.

questions.prompt: On Saint Helena, Jacob's Ladder connects Jamestown to Ladder Hill Fort, and it's all very downhill from here if you're heading back down. How many steps make up this steep staircase?
questions.hint: More than 650, but fewer than 900 steps.
questions.explanation: Jacob's Ladder is a staircase of 699 steps built in 1829 on the site of a former inclined railway, linking Jamestown with Ladder Hill Fort on Saint Helena.

questions.prompt: Amanda McKittrick Ros's writing was so comically overwrought that two famous Oxford authors, J. R. R. Tolkien and C. S. Lewis, would compete to see who could read her prose the longest without doing what?

questions.prompt: The 1967 NFL Championship Game, known as 'The Ice Bowl', was played between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers in a brutal -15°F temperature. How many fans attended this frigid game at Lambeau Field?
questions.hint: The attendance was somewhere between 48,000 and 53,000 fans.
questions.explanation: Despite the extreme cold, 50,861 fans attended the game at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin.

questions.prompt:
Which unusual article does the following describe?

This was an underground organization uncovered in South Korea that authorities alleged was working toward the "liberation" and unification of the Korean peninsula under a pro-North Korean, communist framework. The group was portrayed by the South Korean government as a clandestine network of subversives and spies, and its exposure led to arrests, trials, and was used to justify a broader crackdown on dissidents and left-wing sympathizers during a period of heightened anti-communist sentiment and authoritarian rule in South Korea.
choices: South Korean National Liberation Front Preparation Committee
Committee for the Reconstruction of the Korean Peninsula
National Alliance for Democracy and Unification
questions.hint: The correct answer is not referred to as a 'Party' or 'Alliance' in its official name, but rather as a formal organizational group tied to liberation efforts.

article.title: South Korean National Liberation Front Preparation Committee

questions.explanation: The article describes the South Korean National Liberation Front Preparation Committee, an underground organization that South Korean authorities alleged was a pro-North Korean subversive network, whose discovery led to arrests and trials amid the country's anti-communist crackdowns.

questions.prompt: Hardware disease is a condition in bovines caused by ingesting stray bits of metal, which can puncture a specific stomach chamber. Which chamber of the cow's stomach is primarily affected?
questions.hint: 9 letters, one word; this chamber is nicknamed the 'honeycomb' due to its textured lining.
questions.explanation: Hardware disease occurs when cattle ingest sharp metal objects that lodge in the reticulum, sometimes piercing its wall and causing further complications like damage to the heart.

questions.prompt:
Which unusual article does the following describe?

This spacecraft was launched by a space agency in late 1998 as part of a mission to study the atmosphere and climate of another planet. After traveling for about nine months, the probe was lost during its orbital insertion maneuver in September 1999. An investigation revealed that the failure was caused by a navigation error: one engineering team used imperial units of force while another used metric units, and the discrepancy was never caught. This caused the spacecraft to approach the planet at a much lower altitude than planned, leading to its destruction or loss.
questions.hint: Two of the incorrect choices experienced failures related to landing or parachute deployment, not a navigation error caused by mixing imperial and metric units.
questions.explanation: The Mars Climate Orbiter was lost in September 1999 because of a navigation error caused by one team using English (imperial) units while another used metric units in calculating thruster performance data, leading the spacecraft to fly too close to Mars and likely burn up or crash.

questions.prompt: According to Wikipedia, the article on Toadsuck, Texas describes it as a fake town invented by a gubernatorial candidate one night after having too much of what?
questions.hint: 7 letters, 1 word; it's a common beverage ingredient that impairs judgment when consumed in excess.
questions.explanation: The article explains that Toadsuck, Texas is not a real place, but rather a fictional town that a candidate for Texas governor made up after drinking too much alcohol one night.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a real unusual article about a marathon Senate filibuster that lasted over 24 hours?
choices: Huey Long filibuster of the Revenue Act of 1932
Robert La Follette filibuster of the Aldrich-Vreeland Act
Strom Thurmond filibuster of the Civil Rights Act of 1957
Wayne Morse filibuster of the Tidelands Oil Act
questions.hint: The real article is not about Huey Long or Robert La Follette, both of whom are associated with different pieces of legislation entirely.

article.title: Strom Thurmond filibuster of the Civil Rights Act of 1957

questions.explanation: In 1957, Senator Strom Thurmond set the record for the longest one-person Senate filibuster in history, speaking for over 24 hours in an unsuccessful attempt to block the Civil Rights Act of 1957.
